newsitem.title: ITALY: UN agency chief says food aid under budget strain.
newsitem.headline: UN agency chief says food aid under budget strain.

text.p: U.N. Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO) director general Jacques Diouf said on Tuesday the agency would not have enough cash to fund programmes over the next two years unless it tightened its belt.

Speaking to delegates of the Rome-based agency, Diouf said FAO would have to sign new financial deals or slash operating costs in order to honour commitments laid out in a 186-nation declaration at the World Food Summit last November.
"The aims of the Rome Declaration are ambitious and require substantial resources," Diouf told a meeting of FAO's council.

"But at a time of budget stringencies for governments and international organisations everywhere, we need to be innovative in our search for the funds to implement the summit plan of action," he added.
The council met on Tuesday to vote on a two-year budget for 1998-99 which will is due to be ratification in November.
One cost-cutting measure proposed by Diouf would freeze funds for the next two years at the 1996-97 budget level of $650 million.
Diouf said such budget austerity would force FAO to absorb increased costs of $39 million but cautioned that the agency would also have to consider cutting back on food security programmes.
"The ($650 million) scenario would entail no increase in assessments but carries a price in terms of substantially reduced programme activity..." Diouf said.

He said further lending agreements, similar to those signed earlier this year with the World Bank and the African Development Bank, would be crucial to financing the agency's aid programmes in Africa and Asia.

FAO said on Tuesday its development and security programmes were esential to the livelihood of people living in 29 countries, mainly in sub-Saharan Africa, who continue to face food emegencies despite a rise in global food output in 1996.
